subject: Contract: DPA carveout and telemetry evidence scope — product/security input needed
messages:
From: Laura Chen <laura.chen@optimahealth.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: contracts@optimahealth.com
Date: Wed, 9 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: DPA redlines + telemetry evidence scope (OptimaHealth)

Marcus —

Thanks for the call last week. Attaching our redlined DPA (Optima_DPA_Redlines_v3.pdf) and the list of subprocessors we currently require to be either permitted or excluded (optima_subprocessors_20261208.csv). Two asks from Legal/Compliance:

1) Data-use carveout for analytics exports: we need explicit language that Redwood will only export aggregated product telemetry for operational benchmarking and not export customer PII or full customer payloads to third-party analytics vendors. If you cannot commit to that, we need visibility into what is exported and whether we can segregate Optima's telemetry.

2) Evidence for SOC/contract audits: we need a short playbook of artifacts Redwood can provide to demonstrate telemetry controls and audit logs for a security review (e.g., retention window for logs, audit log examples, KMS access logs, subprocessor attestations). Our external counsel also asked whether the Optima carveout would require an exception approval path or could be handled via a contract-level exhibit.

Can you route this to Product and Security for quick signoff? We are targeting a mid-January contract signature and would like to avoid procurement stalls.

Thanks,
Laura
Laura Chen
Head of Procurement, OptimaHealth

Attachments: Optima_DPA_Redlines_v3.pdf, optima_subprocessors_20261208.csv

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Chen <laura.chen@optimahealth.com>, Julian Lee <julian.lee@strattonlaw.com>, contracts@optimahealth.com
Date: Wed, 9 Dec 2026 11:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Fwd: DPA redlines + telemetry evidence scope (OptimaHealth)

Forwarding Optima's redlines — see attachments. High level: Optima is asking for a firm carveout that telemetry exports to analytics vendors will be aggregated-only and that no customer payloads/PII are sent. They also want a concrete list of audit artifacts we can provide for SOC/contract review.

Olga / Grace — can you confirm the following by EOD Friday (12/11)?
- Security: what specific evidence artifacts and retention windows can we commit to today (audit logs, KMS access, SLA for evidence production)? Any blockers to accepting an "aggregated telemetry only" clause?
- Product: what telemetry fields are currently exported to third-party analytics (names, pseudonymized IDs, model ids, latency), and is there a tenant-level toggle to opt Optima out or downgrade to aggregated metrics only? Timeline for a gating change if needed?

Ben — heads-up to align pricing/legal — if we need engineering work to add tenant-level toggles, procurement may ask for credits / timeline commitments.

I'll own the external comms and legal loop. Laura/Jules — we appreciate a firm list of required artifacts and any required formatting for evidence (PDF exports, Syslog snippets).

--
Marcus
Director, Sales — Enterprise
Redwood Inference

From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Laura Chen <laura.chen@optimahealth.com>, Julian Lee <julian.lee@strattonlaw.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Dec 2026 08:34:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: DPA redlines + telemetry evidence scope (OptimaHealth)

Marcus / team —

Quick summary from Security's side after prelim review of the redline: we can likely accommodate an "aggregated telemetry only" restriction for Optima with the following caveats and deliverables:

- Evidence/Artifacts we can produce today:
  * Audit log export (time-range CSV) showing API request hashes, timestamps, actor IDs (hashed), and model variant metadata (retention: 90 days by default; extended retention available as an add-on).
  * KMS access summary (time-windowed, no key material) for up to 12 months.
  * Subprocessor attestations: for hosted analytics partners we currently have, we can provide SOC2/HIPAA attestations; for other smaller vendors we may only have a security questionnaire response.

- What we cannot commit to today: providing raw customer payloads or full conversation transcripts to analytics vendors. Any clause that implies export of full payloads will need escalation and likely a product change.

- Potential path: support the DPA redline but include an exhibit listing allowable telemetry fields (we'll propose a draft set) and a signoff/exception workflow: Security + Product + Sales sign the exception if a specific subprocessor is required. That avoids a blanket policy exception.

Action items for us:
1) I will draft the "allowable telemetry fields" exhibit (ETA: 2 business days).
2) Confirm retention windows and produce sample audit snippets for Optima's legal (ETA: 3 business days for sanitized samples).
3) If Optima insists on tenant-level opt-out today, Product to advise on technical feasibility / timeline.

Notes: if Product cannot deliver a tenant opt-out within the timeline, we should prepare a commercial mitigation (short-term credits + a documented roadmap milestone).

-Olga
Olga Petrov
Senior Security Architect
Redwood Inference

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Laura Chen <laura.chen@optimahealth.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Dec 2026 13:15:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: DPA redlines + telemetry evidence scope (OptimaHealth)

Thanks Marcus / Olga — technical clarity below.

Current telemetry exported to third-party analytics (summary):
- Event-level metrics: request timestamp, model id (e.g., rw-v1-13b), latency_ms bucket, outcome codes (success/error).
- Aggregates: per-minute token counters, model utilization, error rates.
- Opt-in debug: when customers enable debug, we capture anonymized token-level stats and truncated prompts (masked for PII); this is only enabled for a small percentage of customers and requires explicit opt-in.

Important: we do not persist full customer payloads in analytics exports by default. We store full request/response in internal runtime logs for 30 days (used for debugging and quality). Those logs are access-controlled.

Options and timeline:
- Short term (no infra change): Provide Optima with aggregated-only exports and sanitized audit snippets (Olga will provide sample). This meets the legal ask and does not require code changes.
- Medium term (2–3 sprints): Implement tenant-level telemetry toggle to prevent debug/truncated prompt export and reduce retention for that tenant's runtime logs. Engineering estimate: 4–6 weeks if prioritized.

Product ask for contract language: allow us to ship an exhibit that enumerates the fields and confirms "no raw payloads exported to analytics partners"; include the exception workflow Olga proposed. If Sales needs to offer a delivery commitment, propose a milestone in the SOW for the tenant toggle delivery.

Grace
Grace O'Connor
Product Manager, Observability
Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Laura Chen <laura.chen@optimahealth.com>, Julian Lee <julian.lee@strattonlaw.com>
Cc: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, contracts@optimahealth.com
Date: Fri, 11 Dec 2026 15:04:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: DPA redlines + telemetry evidence scope (OptimaHealth) — proposed path and timelines

Laura / Julian — thank you for the redlines and the subprocessors list. Summary and proposed path below (TL;DR at top).

TL;DR: We can accept an "aggregated telemetry only" carveout for Optima via a contract exhibit that enumerates allowable telemetry fields. Security will provide sanitized audit snippets and KMS access summaries within 3 business days. Product can deliver a tenant-level telemetry toggle in 4–6 weeks if Optima requires an on-platform opt-out; otherwise we will provide aggregated exports immediately. If Optima needs the toggle as a contractual milestone, we can add it to the SOW with a delivery date and commercial mitigation (one-time credit) if timelines slip.

What we will deliver (commitments):
- Security (Olga): draft "Allowable Telemetry Fields" exhibit and sanitized audit snippets (ETA: 2–3 business days).
- Product (Grace): confirmation of current exported fields (as listed below) and engineering ETA for tenant toggle (4–6 weeks if prioritized).
- Sales (Ben / Marcus): if the toggle is required in-contract, propose SOW milestone + limited credit (to be finalized with Legal).

Allowable fields (draft, non-exhaustive): request timestamp, model id, latency_ms group, outcome code, aggregated token counters, error rates. No raw request/response payloads or unmasked user content.

Next steps / owners:
- Olga: send the exhibit draft + one sanitized audit sample to Laura & Julian (ETA: Tue 12/15).
- Grace: confirm resource allocation / sprint for tenant toggle and provide formal ETA (ETA: Mon 12/14).
- Ben: prepare proposed commercial mitigation (credit %) if Optima insists on immediate toggle delivery in-contract (ETA: Tue 12/15).
- Marcus: I will follow up with a consolidated patch to the DPA and a suggested exhibit language for Optima to review (ETA: Tue 12/15).

If that schedule works, we think we can keep Optima on the mid-Jan signature path. If Optima pushes for on-platform enforcement before signing, we will need to negotiate the SOW milestone + commercial accommodation.

Laura — please confirm if the exhibit approach is acceptable or if you need a hard tenant-level toggle before signature.

Thanks all,
Marcus
Director, Sales — Enterprise
Redwood Inference
